newsitem.title: ITALY: Italy employers warn on inflation in second half.
newsitem.headline: Italy employers warn on inflation in second half.

text.p: Italy's employers federation Confindustria warned on Monday that inflation could tick higher in the second half of the year after official data confirmed that annual inflation dipped to 2.2 percent in March.
The warning came from Confindustria's director general Innocenzo Cipolletta while attending a conference.

"We have said that inflation was in decline up to the end of the spring. Up to the middle of the year we believe that inflation will remain low. This is a positive move. Nevertheless, we underline it could resume if not enough attention is paid," said Cipolletta.
"Production costs and, in particular salaries, in 1996 and above all in 1997 are rising at a rate greater than inflation, said Cipolletta.
Earlier today, Italy reported that annual consumer price index inflation in March fell to 2.2 percent from February's year-on-year rate of 2.4 percent.

Italy's Treasury Minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi repeated today that inflation would fall below two percent in April, while he has said that inflation may stabilise at 1.5 percent by the end of the June.
